answers.answer: Keep 4 gems per color and 5 gold. Reveal 3 nobles; the other 7 are permanently removed.
answers.evidence: Token Setup Quick Reference; Noble Tile Mechanics: removed nobles are permanently out.

answers.answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles: two more gems per color and one more noble.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table.

answers.answer: Shuffle the three decks separately; place level 1 at the bottom, level 2 in the middle, level 3 on top. Reveal 4 per level, 12 total. The youngest starts and play goes clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player.

answers.answer: Take three different gems; take two same-color gems with at least four in that supply; reserve one card if holding fewer than three and take gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved card. Neither taking gems then buying nor reserving then buying that card is allowed in one turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “must” perform “exactly one” action; reserved purchases require reservation on a previous turn.

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: “All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.”

answers.answer: Take two green from four, leaving two. You cannot take two red from three. Check the threshold before taking tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure action 2: “at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them”; both gem actions exclude gold.

answers.answer: Twelve temporarily is allowed. Return two, possibly including newly taken gems. Gold counts toward ten.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit allows temporary excess and returning tokens just taken; ten includes gold.

answers.answer: Take one gold and temporarily reach eleven; return one chosen token, possibly that gold, to end at ten. With no gold available, reserve anyway, gain no gold, and remain at ten.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card; Token Hand Limit allows returning newly acquired gold.

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card of any level deck. Do not show a deck reservation to opponents. Only the reserver can eventually purchase it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: face-up or top deck card, without revealing; purchase restricted to reserver.

answers.answer: No reservation is possible with three held, even just to get gold. You cannot discard or exchange one to make room. Purchase is the only way a reserved card leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: maximum three; only purchase removes a card.

answers.answer: Immediately refill the level-2 space from the top of the level-2 deck. A face-up purchase is replaced the same way from its own level. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy. If the corresponding deck is empty, the space remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement applies immediately to face-up purchases/reservations, from the same level; exhausted deck leaves the space empty.

answers.answer: Spend one green and no blue. If bonuses cover everything, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules give this exact blue/green example and allow token-free purchases; bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses leave one blue, one black, one white. Spend the blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. All spent tokens return to supply. Your bonus cards stay with you.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonus discounts, gold substitutes for any gem, spent tokens return to supply; Bonus Stacking: permanent bonuses.

answers.answer: Purchase a face-up market card or your previously reserved card. Place purchased cards face-up before you, grouped by bonus color and staggered with bonuses and prestige values always visible to everyone.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card, including the final arrangement paragraph.

answers.answer: No: tokens, including gold, cannot replace the missing white bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn. Excess bonuses do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: at least the required bonuses from purchased cards, not tokens.

answers.answer: Choose one noble. You cannot take both or refuse all. It uses no action, gives three prestige, and eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after the action.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: automatic, not an action, choose one if multiple, at most one per turn, three points.

answers.answer: Place it face-up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: “Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.”

answers.answer: C and D still act; A does not act again. B is not guaranteed to win because another player can surpass B during the final round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round for equal turns. End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player may be surpassed.

answers.answer: You reach sixteen and trigger the ending because the threshold is fifteen or more. Determine the winner after the current round is complete and turn counts are equal.
answers.evidence: Noble value three; End-Game Trigger: “15 or more”; winner uses final-round totals.

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie at sixteen and B bought nine developments versus ten. C has fewer points. Noble points count. B’s reserved cards are not purchased cards and do not enter the tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner; Tiebreaker uses purchased developments; Prestige Point Sources includes purchased cards and nobles.

answers.answer: Reserved points count toward neither score nor the trigger; their bonuses neither discount purchases nor satisfy nobles until purchased.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: purchased cards. Payment rules: previously purchased cards. Noble Visits: purchased-card bonuses.

answers.answer: No physical blue token is gained. Its permanent blue bonus discounts future purchases and helps qualify for nobles even with zero prestige.
answers.evidence: Cards may be worth zero; Bonus Stacking: bonuses never generate tokens; nobles use purchased-card bonuses.

answers.answer: You cannot buy the blue card: its own bonus is not from a previously purchased card and cannot pay its cost. A newly bought white bonus counts toward a noble at the end of this same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: previously purchased cards. Noble Visits: purchased-card bonuses checked at end of turn.

answers.answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot cover green or yield change. You still owe two green, paid with green tokens and/or two equivalent gold substitutions.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess bonuses give no benefit for that purchase and no change. Gold substitutes for any single gem.

answers.answer: Bonuses are not used up. Taking gems next turn can still yield the other noble at the end of your turn if it remains available. You cannot receive it on an opponent’s intervening turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent; unchosen nobles remain for future turns; visits occur at the end of the player’s turn.

answers.answer: Yes, reserve it despite being unable to buy it. Reserving does not require paying the printed purchase cost. Take one gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card permits face-up cards without a cost payment; payment belongs to the separate purchase action.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or replaced; twelve remain. You take only the one deck card into your hand, with no second replacement card.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: take one card, either face-up or top of a deck. Replacement applies to face-up cards removed from the grid.

answers.answer: The four face-up cards remain available for purchase or reservation. Buying one leaves an empty space because its deck is empty; the other three remain available.
answers.evidence: Purchase/reservation actions allow face-up cards. Card Replacement: exhausted deck leaves the space empty.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the reserved card or take three different gems. Continue until the normal prestige-point ending.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger explicitly states deck or market exhaustion does not end the game; continue remaining legal actions including reserved purchases.

answers.answer: Yes. Take the three and return all three just taken to end with the same ten. No net gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit permits temporary excess and returning “some or all of the tokens they just took.”

answers.answer: A returns the two gold to supply. B takes one on reserving, leaving one gold in supply before token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules return spent gold to supply; reservation takes one gold if available.

answers.answer: Yes, buy the affordable face-up level-3 card now. The purchase action has no requirement to acquire lower levels first.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card allows a face-up card from the grid on payment; the grid includes all three levels.

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble. Your turn ends at eighteen points: twelve plus three plus three. Players still due a turn in the current round continue.
answers.evidence: Noble visits cannot be refused and grant three points; End-Game Trigger completes the current round.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes this turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets an extra turn, since everyone has taken the same number of turns.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round so every player has played the same number of turns.

answers.answer: No replacement noble is revealed: removed nobles are permanently out. The acquired tile goes face-up before its recipient. Two nobles remain in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: removed nobles permanently out; Noble Visits: received tile face-up in front of player.

answers.answer: Emerald green; diamond white; sapphire blue; onyx black; ruby red; gold joker yellow. Ninety developments total: forty level 1, thirty level 2, twenty level 3.
answers.evidence: Components: Tokens and Development Cards tables.

answers.answer: You may pay gold and keep the green. Return the gold payment to supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: gold can substitute for any single gem token and spent gold returns to supply.

answers.answer: Yes. Take one from each, leaving zero red, one blue, two green. The four-token minimum applies only to the two-of-the-same-color action.
answers.evidence: Actions 1 and 2: three different colors requires one from each; four-token threshold belongs to same-color action.

answers.answer: Directly exchanging gold for red is neither a listed action nor a use granted by the joker rule. During a purchase, gold substitutes for any single gem token and is returned to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists exactly four choices; Gold Token Specifics limits the substitution description to purchasing a card.

answers.answer: You must perform one of the four actions; voluntary passing with legal actions available is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: player “must” perform “exactly one” listed action.
